The Children's Peace Monument, located in Hiroshima, Japan, commemorates Sadako Sasaki and thousands of child victims of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima. Sadako Sasaki died of leukemia from radiation of the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945. 

Nuclear weapons were first used in combat in August 1945, when two fission bombs were dropped on Japan. The development of nuclear weapons involved scientific breakthroughs made during the 1930s and collaboration between the United States, the United Kingdom, and Canada during World War II. The Soviet Union also developed nuclear weapons shortly after the United States.

Jacob Beser, a lieutenant in the United States Army Air Forces, served as a radar specialist aboard the "Enola Gay" on August 6, 1945, when it dropped the Little Boy atomic bomb on Hiroshima. He was also a crewmember aboard "Bockscar" when the Fat Man bomb was dropped on Nagasaki three days later. 

The Fat Man bomb was detonated over Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, marking the second and only other time a nuclear weapon has been used in warfare. The bomb was built using plutonium from the Hanford Site and dropped from the Boeing B-29 Superfortress "Bockscar", piloted by Major Charles W. Sweeney. Vice Admiral Frederick Lincoln "Dick" Ashworth served as the weaponeer on the B-29 "Bockscar" for the Fat Man mission.
